primaryText: John went to his favorite music store to buy a piano. He had frequented the store for many years. He was excited that he could finally buy a piano. He arrived just as the store was closing for the day.
discourseSegments: John went to his favorite music store to buy a piano.
He had frequented the store for many years.
He was excited that he could finally buy a piano.
He arrived just as the store was closing for the day.
comment: Intuitively more coherent than (2).

primaryText: John went to his favorite music store to buy a piano. It was a store John had frequented for many years. He was excited that he could finally buy a piano. It was closing just as John arrived.
discourseSegments: John went to his favorite music store to buy a piano.
It was a store John had frequented for many years.
He was excited that he could finally buy a piano.
It was closing just as John arrived.
comment: Less coherent than (1): the discourse flips back and forth among several entities.

primaryText: Terry really goofs sometimes. Yesterday was a beautiful day and he was excited about trying out his new sailboat. He wanted Tony to join him on a sailing expedition. He called him at 6 AM. He was sick and furious at being woken up so early.
discourseSegments: Terry really goofs sometimes.
Yesterday was a beautiful day and he was excited about trying out his new sailboat.
He wanted Tony to join him on a sailing expedition.
He called him at 6 AM.
He was sick and furious at being woken up so early.
comment: The pronoun in (e) misleads: Terry has been the center of attention, and only 'sick' forces Tony.

primaryText: Terry really goofs sometimes. Yesterday was a beautiful day and he was excited about trying out his new sailboat. He wanted Tony to join him on a sailing expedition. He called him at 6 AM. Tony was sick and furious at being woken up so early. He told Terry to get lost and hung up. Of course, he hadn't intended to upset Tony.
discourseSegments: Terry really goofs sometimes.
Yesterday was a beautiful day and he was excited about trying out his new sailboat.
He wanted Tony to join him on a sailing expedition.
He called him at 6 AM.
Tony was sick and furious at being woken up so early.
He told Terry to get lost and hung up.
Of course, he hadn't intended to upset Tony.
comment: (f) and (g) exhibit the same misdirection as (3d) and (3e): the focus has shifted to Tony.

primaryText: Terry really goofs sometimes. Yesterday was a beautiful day and he was excited about trying out his new sailboat. He wanted Tony to join him on a sailing expedition. He called him at 6 AM. Tony was sick and furious at being woken up so early. He told Terry to get lost and hung up. Of course, Terry hadn't intended to upset Tony.
discourseSegments: Terry really goofs sometimes.
Yesterday was a beautiful day and he was excited about trying out his new sailboat.
He wanted Tony to join him on a sailing expedition.
He called him at 6 AM.
Tony was sick and furious at being woken up so early.
He told Terry to get lost and hung up.
Of course, Terry hadn't intended to upset Tony.
comment: The confusion of (4g) is avoided by the name.

primaryText: Susan gave Betsy a pet hamster. She reminded her that such hamsters were quite shy.
discourseSegments: Susan gave Betsy a pet hamster.
She reminded her that such hamsters were quite shy.
comment: A priori either Susan or Betsy might be the Cb of (b).

primaryText: Susan gave Betsy a pet hamster. She reminded her that such hamsters were quite shy. She asked Betsy whether she liked the gift.
discourseSegments: Susan gave Betsy a pet hamster.
She reminded her that such hamsters were quite shy.
She asked Betsy whether she liked the gift.
comment: Susan continued as Cb.

primaryText: Susan gave Betsy a pet hamster. She reminded her that such hamsters were quite shy. Betsy told her that she really liked the gift.
discourseSegments: Susan gave Betsy a pet hamster.
She reminded her that such hamsters were quite shy.
Betsy told her that she really liked the gift.
comment: Susan merely retained as Cb; better than (9) although it changes grammatical position.

primaryText: Susan gave Betsy a pet hamster. She reminded her that such hamsters were quite shy. Susan asked her whether she liked the gift.
discourseSegments: Susan gave Betsy a pet hamster.
She reminded her that such hamsters were quite shy.
Susan asked her whether she liked the gift.
comment: Marked decrease in acceptability from (7) to (10).

primaryText: Susan gave Betsy a pet hamster. She reminded her that such hamsters were quite shy. She told Susan that she really liked the gift.
discourseSegments: Susan gave Betsy a pet hamster.
She reminded her that such hamsters were quite shy.
She told Susan that she really liked the gift.
comment: For many people completely unacceptable.

primaryText: Susan is a fine friend. She gives people the most wonderful presents. She just gave Betsy a wonderful bottle of wine. She told her it was quite rare. She knows a lot about wine.
discourseSegments: Susan is a fine friend.
She gives people the most wonderful presents.
She just gave Betsy a wonderful bottle of wine.
She told her it was quite rare.
She knows a lot about wine.
comment: Strong preference for Susan, realized in subject position in (d).

primaryText: Susan is a fine friend. She gives people the most wonderful presents. She just gave Betsy a wonderful bottle of wine. She told her it was quite rare. Wine collecting gives her expertise that's fun to share.
discourseSegments: Susan is a fine friend.
She gives people the most wonderful presents.
She just gave Betsy a wonderful bottle of wine.
She told her it was quite rare.
Wine collecting gives her expertise that's fun to share.
comment: The preference for Susan holds regardless of syntactic position in (e), so it is not parallelism.

primaryText: Have you seen the new toys the kids got this weekend? Stuffed animals must really be out of fashion. Susie prefers the green plastic tugboat to the teddy bear. Tommy likes it better than the bear too, but only because the silly thing is bigger.
discourseSegments: Have you seen the new toys the kids got this weekend?
Stuffed animals must really be out of fashion.
Susie prefers the green plastic tugboat to the teddy bear.
Tommy likes it better than the bear too, but only because the silly thing is bigger.
comment: 'The silly thing' is the boat, the most likely Cb.

primaryText: Have you seen the new toys the kids got this weekend? Stuffed animals must really be out of fashion. Susie prefers the green plastic tugboat to the teddy bear. Tommy likes it better than the bear too, although the silly thing is bigger.
discourseSegments: Have you seen the new toys the kids got this weekend?
Stuffed animals must really be out of fashion.
Susie prefers the green plastic tugboat to the teddy bear.
Tommy likes it better than the bear too, although the silly thing is bigger.
comment: Pragmatics prefers the bear as 'the silly thing', in conflict with the boat's being the most likely Cb.

primaryText: He has been acting quite odd. He called up Mike yesterday. John wanted to meet him urgently.
discourseSegments: He has been acting quite odd.
He called up Mike yesterday.
John wanted to meet him urgently.
comment: Presumed within a segment centered on John; the only interpretation takes 'John' in (c) as a second John, and even then the sequence is very odd.

primaryText: John has been acting quite odd. He called up Mike yesterday. Mike was studying for his driver's test. He was annoyed by John's call.
discourseSegments: John has been acting quite odd.
He called up Mike yesterday.
Mike was studying for his driver's test.
He was annoyed by John's call.
comment: The intervening (c) shifts the center from John to Mike; per Gordon, Grosz, and Gilliom (1993), (16d) without (c) is not as bad as (15c).

primaryText: My dog is getting quite obstreperous. I took him to the vet the other day. The mangy old beast always hates these visits.
discourseSegments: My dog is getting quite obstreperous.
I took him to the vet the other day.
The mangy old beast always hates these visits.
comment: Adapted from Sidner (1979); the Cb is realized by a definite description that conveys more than reference.

primaryText: I'm reading The French Lieutenant's Woman. The book, which is Fowles's best, was a bestseller last year.
discourseSegments: I'm reading The French Lieutenant's Woman.
The book, which is Fowles's best, was a bestseller last year.

primaryText: The house appeared to have been burgled. The door was ajar. The furniture was in disarray.
discourseSegments: The house appeared to have been burgled.
The door was ajar.
The furniture was in disarray.
comment: The house is realized but not directly realized in (b); the door ranks above it in Cf(b).

primaryText: John has been having a lot of trouble arranging his vacation. He cannot find anyone to take over his responsibilities. He called up Mike yesterday to work out a plan. Mike has annoyed him a lot recently. He called John at 5 AM on Friday last week.
discourseSegments: John has been having a lot of trouble arranging his vacation.
He cannot find anyone to take over his responsibilities.
He called up Mike yesterday to work out a plan.
Mike has annoyed him a lot recently.
He called John at 5 AM on Friday last week.
comment: Annotated CONTINUE, RETAIN, SHIFT at (c), (d), (e).

primaryText: The Vice-President of the United States is also President of the Senate. Historically, he is the President's key man in negotiations with Congress. He is required to be 35 years old.
discourseSegments: The Vice-President of the United States is also President of the Senate.
Historically, he is the President's key man in negotiations with Congress.
He is required to be 35 years old.
comment: Value-free interpretation of the description.

primaryText: The Vice-President of the United States is also President of the Senate. Right now, he's the president's key person in negotiations with Congress. As Ambassador to China, he handled many tricky negotiations, so he is well prepared for this job.
discourseSegments: The Vice-President of the United States is also President of the Senate.
Right now, he's the president's key person in negotiations with Congress.
As Ambassador to China, he handled many tricky negotiations, so he is well prepared for this job.
comment: Value-loaded interpretation of the description.

primaryText: A: The Vice-President of the U.S. is also President of the Senate. B: I thought he played some important role in the House. A: He did, but that was before he was the Vice-President.
discourseSegments: A: The Vice-President of the U.S. is also President of the Senate.
B: I thought he played some important role in the House.
A: He did, but that was before he was the Vice-President.
comment: (b) prefers the value-free interpretation but allows the value-loaded one (c) needs.

primaryText: John thinks that the telephone is a nuisance. He curses it every day. He doesn't realize that it is an invention that changed the world.
discourseSegments: John thinks that the telephone is a nuisance.
He curses it every day.
He doesn't realize that it is an invention that changed the world.
comment: Christine Nakatani's example: (b) prefers value-loaded, (c) requires value-free.

primaryText: Her husband is kind to her. No, he isn't. The man you're referring to isn't her husband.
discourseSegments: Her husband is kind to her.
No, he isn't. The man you're referring to isn't her husband.
comment: Kripke (1977): the Cb of (b) is the husband.

primaryText: Her husband is kind to her. He is kind to her but he isn't her husband.
discourseSegments: Her husband is kind to her.
He is kind to her but he isn't her husband.
comment: Kripke (1977): the Cb of (b) is the lover.

primaryText: I haven't seen Jeff for several days. Carl thinks he's studying for his exams, but I think he went to the Cape with Linda.
discourseSegments: I haven't seen Jeff for several days.
Carl thinks he's studying for his exams,
but I think he went to the Cape with Linda.
comment: Sidner's actor focus makes Carl the leading candidate for 'he' in (c); on the centering account Jeff is the Cb at (b).
